outcome: length of second stage of labor
cohort: 2123 low-risk women receiving midwife-led care and age- and parity-matched low-risk women with spontaneous vaginal birth overseen by an obstetrician-led team
finding: Midwife-led care for low-risk women was associated with a significant decrease in interventions, including oxytocin use, medical pain relief, artificial rupture of membranes, and episiotomies, without negatively impacting maternal or neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Midwife-led care was associated with fewer interventions, but mode of delivery (spontaneous vaginal birth vs. assisted deliveries) was not significantly different between groups.
